text:
anya: Quick update from the embeddings bring-up: ran the initial eval suite on `openembed-v2` (FP16) vs our current prod `redwood-embed-1`.
kevin: curious—what datasets? recall@k or cluster metrics?
anya: short summary: USE benchmark subset (10k pairs), internal product clusters (docs from kb), and synthetic paraphrase set. Primary metrics: recall@1/5/10, mean reciprocal rank, and silhouette score for clustering.
sofia: nice. numbers?
anya: paste of the main output:
```
Model              R@1    R@5    R@10   MRR    Silhouette
redwood-embed-1    0.62   0.79   0.85   0.71  0.38
openembed-v2       0.59   0.77   0.83   0.68  0.33
openembed-v2-4bit  0.54   0.72   0.80   0.63  0.30
```
sofia: looks like a small but consistent drop, worse with 4-bit quant.
matt: did you normalize vectors / use cosine? that's usually important for R@k.
anya: yes, all runs used L2-normalized vectors with cosine sim. Also tried no-norm; patterns similar but lower absolute scores.
kevin: can you share the eval config? batch sizes, pooling strategy?
anya: config snippet:
```
pooling: mean
seq_trunc: 512
batch_size: 256
index: faiss.IndexFlatIP (normalized vectors)
quant: bits=4, scheme=nf4
```
kevin: interesting. For the cluster silhouette drop, any evidence of cluster collapse or increased intra-cluster distances?
anya: t-SNE quick look shows tighter global spread for redwood-embed and slight overlap for openembed-v2. Computed avg intra-cluster dist increased ~8% for openembed.
sofia: can we split by domain? product docs vs support KB vs paraphrase set? might be domain mismatch.
anya: yes, breakdown:
- product docs: R@1 delta -0.04
- support KB: R@1 delta -0.01
- paraphrase set: R@1 delta -0.08
sofia: paraphrase worst — openembed seems weaker on synonyms paraphrase generalization.
matt: do we have any evals with longer contexts? maybe seq_trunc 512 hurts.
anya: tried 1024 for a subset; recall improved by ~0.01 for openembed but not enough to match redwood.
kevin: can we try float16 quant (quant aware) or hybrid: embeddings stored as 4-bit PQ but with float16 centroids?
anya: good idea. I'll run hybrid PQ and also try post-hoc calibration (mean-centering + whitening) we use in other stacks.
anya: scheduled two jobs: hybrid-pq (estimated 6h) and whitening+re-eval (2h). I'll post results.
eval-bot: CI job queued: eval/embeddings/hybrid-pq-1782590123 started (job id: ev-9921)
sofia: also add a retrieval downstream test (actual RAG QA F1) — sometimes R@k doesn't tell full story.
anya: yup adding downstream RAG on 500 queries, will include latency and index size. initial index size: openembed-v2-4bit ~12GB vs redwood ~38GB.
matt: thanks. if hybrid PQ gets R@1 within 0.01 and preserves 3x reduction, that's promising.
kevin: sounds good. tagging @infra to make sure the FAISS job gets node with 768GB RAM.
anya: thanks all — will update thread when jobs finish. :clock1:
eval-bot: CI job completed: eval/embeddings/whitening-1782590123 finished (ev-9922) — results uploaded to /evals/1782590123/whitening.json
anya: uploaded whitening results: whitening recovered ~0.02 R@1 for openembed-v2 (paraphrase improved most). still below redwood but gap narrowed.
sofia: progress. final comparison should factor cost/latency and index ops. will wait for hybrid PQ results.
matt: small note: add a test for cosine vs inner-product in FAISS — we used IP but with normalized vectors, equivalently cosine; just sanity.
anya: added that to job. will ping when hybrid is done.
